articles.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Winery Lawsuit That Revealed Abuse Allegations
articles.summary: Brad Pitt has settled his legal battle with ex-wife Angelina Jolie over the sale of her stake in the couple’s winery in France. Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, accusing her of selling her 50% share in Château Miraval to a subsidiary of Stoli, the Russian spirits company, without Pitt’s approval.
body: “We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” representatives for Jolie and Pitt said in a statement on Wednesday. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed. Pitt has also sued Yuri Shefler, the Russian-born billionaire who owns the Stoli Group. That portion of the litigation is ongoing.

Pitt and Jolie bought the Miraval estate in 2008, and were married there in 2014. They invested tens of millions of dollars in the 1,300-acre property in order to turn Château Miraval into a profitable rosé brand.

Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, and the fate of the winery has been in dispute ever since. Pitt has argued that the company was his “passion,” that he poured his energies into making it a success, and that Jolie has forced him into an unworkable arrangement with Stoli, a competitor. In a cross-complaint filed in 2022, Jolie accused Pitt attempting to seize control from her and of “looting” it for other ventures.

articles.title: King Crimson Original Drummer Michael Giles Dies at 84
articles.summary: Michael Giles, whose drumming on King Crimson’s legendary debut album brought fire and abandon to an already wild and innovative sound, has died, according to a post on the band’s website. No cause of death was announced; he was 84.
body: Born in 1942, Giles — pictured above, bottom right, with Crimson in 1969 — hailed from Bournemouth on England’s south coast, along with Crimson cofounders Robert Fripp (far left) and Greg Lake (top). In 1967, he formed a group with his brother Peter and Fripp called, naturally enough, Giles, Giles and Fripp. The trio released an album titled “The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp” the following year, to extremely modest commercial results. However, the album laid the groundwork for King Crimson, which Giles formed late in 1968 with Fripp, vocalist/ bassist Lake, multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald and lyricist Peter Sinfield.

Its influence was profound, and can be heard everywhere from the music of fellow prog-rock travelers Yes and Genesis as well as David Bowie, Roxy Music and countless later acolytes like Tool and the Mars Volta; its song “20 th Century Schizoid Man” was famously sampled by Kanye West on his 2010 single “Power.”
Giles’ wild drumming was key to the band’s first lineup, embellishing its classical-tinged sound with innovative, thunderous drum rolls and lightning-fast rhythms.

articles.title: NBC Plans to Give Thanksgiving Parade Ads Extra Run After Macy’s Postponement
articles.summary: NBC has a Thanksgiving Week present for advertisers scheduled to appear in the now-postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The network plans to run commercials from sponsors of the event twice this week — once when the 2026 parade airs on Saturday and once on Thursday, when the network will run a…
body: Macy’s and NBC decided to postpone the parade to Saturday, November 28, citing extreme wind conditions and inclement weather expected on Thursday. Many of the signature balloons used in the parade cannot be controlled properly during high wind speeds. The network said it is “committed to ensuring this remains a high-priority opportunity for our clients with both the reach and scale of tomorrow’s re-airing and the original live telecast on Saturday.”

NBC has many reasons to keep advertisers in the parade happy. The cost of a 30-second commercial in the parade is up 15% to 20% over last year, according to Guideline, a tracker of ad spending, when NBC was able to charge between $900,000 and $1 million per unit. Those figures would indicate that a 30-second spot in the 2026 parade could cost between$1.03 million and $1.2 million. Ad spend on the event is pacing about 25% to 30% ahead of last year, according to Guideline. The parade snared more than $88.7 million in ads last year, the company says.

articles.title: ‘The Hawk’ Starring Will Ferrell Canceled After One Season at Netflix
articles.summary: “The Hawk” has hit the rough. Netflix has canceled the golf comedy series after just one season. The series, which starred Will Ferrell in his first regular TV role since “SNL,” originally debuted on the streamer back in July.
body: The official logline for “The Hawk” states “Lonnie Hawkins (Ferrell),2004’s number one golfer, struggles on the back nine of his career to recapture his magic. His body says retire, but his heart says he’s not done yet. His ex-wife and his son Lance, golf’s new golden boy, know he’s through. But with one more major to win to complete golf’s Grand Slam, Lonnie refuses to believe he’s anything other than one stroke away from the greatest comeback in golf history.”
Along with Ferrell, the cast included Molly Shannon, Jimmy Tatro, Fortune Feimster, Luke Wilson, Chris Parnell, Katelyn Tarver and David Hornsby.

Ferrell co-created the series with Harper Steele and Chris Hency. All three were executive producers along with Jessica Elbaum and Alix Taylor for Ferrell’s Gloria Sanchez Productions; Rian Johnson, Ram Bergman and Nena Rodrigue for T-Street; David Gordon Green; and Andrew Guest.

articles.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
articles.summary: The musician, who co-wrote some of the band's biggest hits, had been treated for prostate cancer.
body: Andy Taylor, the guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65.
Born in Tynemouth, he co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film; and also worked with artists like Robert Palmer, Rod Stewart and Belinda Carlisle.
In a statement, his bandmates said Taylor had fought "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer" and "passed away peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23 November".
His wife, Tracey, said the musician "was the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day".

articles.title: Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a true Wild Boy
articles.summary: How a wayward child from the north-east of England made it with the world's biggest band.
body: Andy Taylor, who has died aged 65, was the wild boy of Duran Duran.
In the early 1980s, the pop legends sold over 100 million records and dominated the charts in both Britain and the United States.
But success came at a cost. For Taylor, global superstardom became a cocaine and alcohol fuelled nightmare that left him burnt out and battling clinical depression.
"For sure, we paraded around in our fast cars with beautiful models on yachts in the south of France without needing to pay the bill," he later wrote.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Released by Steelers After ‘Pat McAfee Show’ Appearance
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday, after comments he made about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on the ESPN’s show.
body: Rodgers responded by taking an excused absence from the club, then used the unexpected time off to go on McAfee and repeatedly call the 62-year-old McCarthy’s mental state into question.
Rodgers told McAfee he found out about the surprise decision while on the phone with teammates, including tight end Pat Freiermuth.

It was just the start of a blistering offensive from Rodgers, who painted McCarthy — whom he played under during a long successful run in Green Bay earlier in their careers — as a leader woefully out of touch.

He described a quarterback meeting last Wednesday with McCarthy arriving late, sat down “and within 10 minutes began snoring,” woke up and nodded off again minutes later, then eventually “walks out of the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers also said McCarthy missed an offensive meeting Thursday, missed a walkthrough Friday and a morning meeting Saturday while not holding a team meeting that night.

articles.title: UK Town of Culture bid withdrawn in Strabane after it causes 'great division'
articles.summary: The County Tyrone town was shortlisted as one of 15 possible locations for the inaugural UK Town of Culture 2028, with the chance to win £3m.
body: A competition that is supposed to celebrate local towns has been rejected by a council after it caused "great division" over its UK title.
However, the local council voted not to go ahead with the bid on Wednesday with one councillor claiming it "has the potential to be a disaster for Strabane - for community relations".
The motion, which was put forward by independent councillors, was backed by the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) and Sinn Féin.

A report prepared for councillors said that money had come from a £60,000 Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) grant, and would need to be repaid if the bid did not make it to the final submission stage.

articles.title: BBC appeals against decision to allow Trump's $10bn lawsuit to go ahead
articles.summary: The US president is suing the BBC over the way Panorama edited a speech he gave in 2021.
body: The BBC has lodged an "urgent" appeal against a US judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.6bn) lawsuit against the corporation to go ahead.
The US president is suing the BBC for defamation over the way an episode of Panorama edited a speech he gave in January 2021, shortly before the riot at the US Capitol.
Earlier this month, a federal judge in Florida ruled that the defamation case could proceed after the BBC sought to dismiss it.

The BBC has now filed an appeal with a higher court, saying there is a "complete lack of evidence" that anyone in Florida accessed the programme, and that the broadcaster made "rigorous and systematic efforts to prevent access to the documentary" in the US.

articles.title: With ‘Guarding Stars,’ Jared Padalecki Finally Takes A Break From All That Action
articles.summary: The 'Walker' and 'Supernatural' star enjoys a change of pace in Netflix's latest romantic comedy, based on Katherine Center's 'The Bodyguard.'
body: Jared Padalecki has been steadily employed on television since his days on aughts classic Gilmore Girls, so it’d be easy to assume that playing an actor in the new Netflix holiday offering Guarding Stars would be second nature. But the 44-year-old, who also produces the movie, found the role to be more difficult than he’d expected.

It’s not as though Padalecki is claiming to fly completely under-the-radar. He admits that he’ll often encounter people in public who stop him to share their love for Supernatural or Gilmore Girls, but he’s still able to go to his son’s games or his daughter’s field hockey practices. It helps, certainly, that he and his wife, actress and fellow Guarding Stars producer Genevieve Padalecki, live in a ranch outside Austin, Texas, rather than in Los Angeles.

Guarding Stars, released on the streamer on Nov. 18, is based on Katherine Center’s romance novel The Bodyguard and features a delightful role reversal. Rather than Padalecki, who’s spent much of his adult life starring in action-driven projects, as the dutiful protector, his character Jack finds himself under the care of bodyguard Hannah Brooks, played by Leighton Meester.

articles.title: With HBO Series ‘Scams for a Better Tomorrow,’ Oobah Butler Has a Language for Your Frustration
articles.summary: The former Vice provocateur's five-part HBO series cons the wellness, tech and music industries to help make viewers "feel less f***ing insane" in modern times.
body: “I think the problem is, whenever you try and pin yourself down as one, the other one feels intriguing,” Butler told The Hollywood Reporter in an interview this week. “I don’t know. I think at the heart of all of it is some sort of truth-seeking. And I’m trying to learn something through using satire, which I think there’s a massive tradition of in both of our countries.”

In 2013, that show took Dennis Rodman to North Korea to meet Kim Jong Un for some basketball diplomacy. While Butler, more than a decade later, doesn’t quite top that bizarre feat in his initial run, he does carry the torch, using his charm, wit and an alarmingly natural fearlessness to finagle his way into the top echelons of U.S. industries and get his satirical products in front of some notable gatekeepers, including the New York Times wine critic and Theranos’ former chief creative officer. It’s a ruse, but it takes the kind of steely nerve that makes great journalism.
